title: RFC 9457 Problem Details for HTTP APIs
description: Canonical error envelope every WALTEUR-built HTTP API MUST return on 4xx/5xx, with media type application/problem+json. Supersedes RFC 7807 (obsoleted by RFC 9457, July 2023). The five standard members are 'type', 'status', 'title', 'detail', 'instance'; problem-type extension members (e.g. 'errors', 'balance', 'invalid_params') are permitted alongside them. A bare {} validates because RFC 9457 §3.1 makes every standard member optional, but WALTEUR's house rule REQUIRES 'type' and 'title' (see required[]) so clients can switch on a stable problem identifier rather than a localised string.

type.description: A URI reference (RFC 3986) that identifies the problem TYPE. SHOULD resolve to human-readable documentation. When absent it defaults to 'about:blank', which means 'no semantics beyond the HTTP status'. WALTEUR requires it explicitly so two distinct failures never collapse onto about:blank.

status.description: The HTTP status code (RFC 9110) generated by the origin server for this occurrence. Advisory only — the actual response status is authoritative — but when present it MUST equal that status.

title.description: A short, human-readable, NON-localised summary of the problem type. MUST NOT change from occurrence to occurrence of the same 'type' (except for localisation). This is for humans; machines switch on 'type'.

detail.description: A human-readable explanation specific to THIS occurrence of the problem. Safe to vary per occurrence. MUST NOT leak secrets, stack traces, or PII.

instance.description: A URI reference identifying the specific occurrence of the problem. May be used to request a more detailed problem report (e.g. a trace/correlation id endpoint).

errors.description: OPTIONAL problem-type extension: a list of per-field / per-parameter validation failures. Use for 400/422 validation responses so clients can map failures to inputs.

detail.description: Human-readable description of this specific validation failure.

pointer.description: RFC 6901 JSON Pointer into the request body identifying the offending member, e.g. '/items/3/quantity'.

parameter.description: Name of the offending query/path/header parameter (use when the failure is not in the JSON body).

code.description: Stable machine-readable sub-code for this field error, e.g. 'REQUIRED', 'OUT_OF_RANGE'.

examples.title: Insufficient funds
examples.detail: Your account balance of 30 is below the requested withdrawal of 50.
